key_insight: Dense, low-porosity Fe-based amorphous coatings offer better long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces their friction coefficient and wear rate.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray processing and service humidity should be considered together when designing Fe-based amorphous coatings for corrosion and wear protection of Q235 steel.
method: Deposited Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examined droplet morphology, lamellar structure, and coating defects.
Tested corrosion and tribological behavior under different humidity conditions using Si3N4 balls.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that greater porosity correlates with poorer long-term corrosion resistance and that friction coefficient and wear rate decrease as humidity increases.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance values or humidity ranges, limiting selection of processing and operating conditions.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
